newsitem.title: CHINA: Tomei says not in stake sale talks.
newsitem.headline: Tomei says not in stake sale talks.

text.p: Tomei International (Holdings) Ltd said on Wednesday TCL Electronics Group had contacted the company some time ago to explore business opportunities but added it was not in talks to sell a Tomei stake to TCL.

"Neither Semi-Tech nor Tomei is in negotiations with any party regarding the acquisition or disposal of shares in Tomei at the present time," Tomei said in a joint statement with Semi-Tech (Global) Co Ltd.

The companies said they made the statement in response to a report saying TCL was studying a proposal to acquire a controlling stake in Tomei and to inject a television making and distributing joint venture with Luks Industrial Co Ltd into Tomei at a price of HK$2 billion.

The report also suggested the deal might result in Semi-Tech becoming a minority shareholder of Tomei from a major shareholder, and that part of Luks' stake in the venture would be converted into Tomei shares and into cash, the statement said.
"There are for the time being no negotiations or agreements or contemplation relating to the matters as described in the article," the statement said.

Luks Industrial Co Ltd said in a separate statement that "there is at the present no negotiation or agreement by the company relating to the conversion of the company's stake in the TV joint venture as described in the article."
Luks holds a 38 percent minority stake in the TV joint venture with TCL, a company which has a strong sales network in China.
Trading in shares of Semi-Tech, Tomei and Luks resumed on Wednesday after a one-day trading suspension.
Luks shares fell HK$0.06 to HK$1.20 in early trade.
Semi-Tech shares rose HK$0.10 to HK$11.50.
Tomei shares gained HK$0.02 to HK$0.65.
